messages:
morgan: Heads-up — saw a few tenant incidents where prefetch spiked and then the GPU stalled for ~200-400ms. Looks correlated with the new aggressive prefetch credits we rolled out.
ravi: can you paste the query/trace? was it during a big batch or lots of small chat requests?
sofia: i grabbed flamegraphs — CPU was busy in prefetch worker threads, then GPU queued up and got underfed. suspect credit overcommit + kv-cache growth.
morgan: short dump:
```
prefetch_credit_used=1200
prefetch_credit_limit=1000
kv_cache_entries=1.8M
slot_wait_ns=360000000
```
chris: oh ok that explains it — credits > limit allowed by soft-credits path, so we kick off prefetches even while eviction is lagging. leads to IO + staging pressure.
jen: tl;dr: prefetch should be stall-aware. when residency has high churn, reduce prefetch window or borrow from a backpressure pool.
ravi: propose API: each tenant gets two credit buckets: steady and burst. steady is enforced strictly; burst is allowed but decremented on GPU stall events. if burst goes to 0, we fallback to synchronous load.
sofia: +1. also we should hook allocator's "resident_growth" signal to decrement burst credits proactively.
morgan: rough config idea:
```yaml
prefetch:
  steady_credits: 256
  burst_credits: 1024
  stall_decrement: 64  # credits removed per stall event
  stall_threshold_ms: 50
```
chris: question: who emits stall events? runtime or evictor?
sofia: runtime - it has visibility into inflight queue lengths and gpu idle time. evictor can annotate events when eviction latency spikes.
jen: telemetry: add `prefetch_credit_rejects` counter, `prefetch_stall_events`, and `stall_time_ms` histogram. need tag by tenant, model, and route.
morgan: perf concern: checking credits on hot path adds cost. make checks in the prefetch scheduler not in every prefetch call. scheduler runs per-microbatch.
ravi: tradeoffs: stricter steady credits reduces cold-start latency but could increase on-demand miss rate. burst helps latency but risks stalls — that's why decrement on stall events.
chris: implementation sketch: extend PrefetchPolicy interface with `OnStall(event)` and `OnResidentGrowth(delta)`. default impl handles buckets and timers.
sofia: want a graceful fallback: when burst exhausted, prefetch returns a token to caller that causes immediate synchronous page fetch (no prefetch). avoids building up queued prefetch IO.
jen: experiment plan:
- implement policy behind feature flag `prefetch_self_tuning_v2`
- canary 1% tenants for 24h with telemetry
- compare p95 latency, GPU busy ratio, and prefetch IO ops
- A/B: steady-only vs steady+burst
morgan: sounds good. need an estimation of complexity/time. chris/sofia, you up for a quick RFC PR?
chris: i can draft RFC today. will include API surface and backpressure counters. target for review EOD tomorrow.
sofia: i'll prototype the allocator hook and add unit tests for decrement logic.
ravi: add a simple simulator script to test pathological workloads (tiny requests, long kv-evict delays). can use existing loadgen.
experiment-bot: experiment created: prefetch_self_tuning_v2 (flag id: ex-pre-842). rollout plan: 1% -> 5% -> 20% with automatic rollback on stall_rate>0.5%.
ci-bot: created a canary job template: `canary/prefetch-selftune-v2` — includes perf counters and flamegraph dump step.
jen: one more ops concern: make sure we expose a per-tenant override to pin burst=0 for sensitive customers.
morgan: good call.
sofia: Also note: we should cap global aggregate burst so one noisy tenant can't exhaust IO. add `global_burst_quota`.
ravi: ok ok final checklist:
- [ ] RFC PR (chris)
- [ ] allocator hook prototype (sofia)
- [ ] simulator + load plan (ravi)
- [ ] telemetry + dashboards (jen)
- [ ] feature flag + canary infra (ci-bot/experiment-bot)
morgan: thanks — i'll follow up with RFC link once chris posts it. :thumbsup:
chris: posted: https://redwood.internal/rfcs/7012345800-prefetch-self-tuning-v2 — PTAL
morgan: reading now, will comment.
sofia: leaving notes in the RFC re: unit tests and eviction signal semantics.
jen: i'll create dashboards after initial canary metrics land.
morgan: cheers, closing thread for now. ping if you hit blockers.
